PullRequest.Title: Add Chat Customizations protocol handler

## Summary

Adds a `chat-customizations` protocol handler that opens a requested Chat Customizations page and optionally populates its search field. The handler supports Discover, Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, MCP Servers, Plugins, Tools, and Migrations, with normalized human-readable page names.

Includes VS Code Insiders URL examples and documents that Discover requires `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled`.

Fixes #340688

Test plan: #340689

## Validation

- Passed: `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed: `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed: `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationUrlHandler.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagement.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementSectionRegistry.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/pluginListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/toolsListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationUrlHandler.test.ts`
- Passed: `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationUrlHandler.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.test.ts` (8 tests)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The selection-to-snapshot and query-to-search call paths, distinct cancellation tokens, 400 ms overlap window, default legacy-marketplace setting, and lack of in-flight coalescing are all explicit in the repository. Exact cost varies with cache warmth, configured marketplace count, and request duration, which is why severity is low.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Marketplace HTTP requests (and clone-backed marketplace discovery for private repositories)
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold deep link, the work grows from one fetch per configured plugin marketplace to two concurrent fetches per marketplace when the initial snapshot takes longer than the 400 ms search delay.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Duplicated network/subprocess work and additional contention before plugin search results appear
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening/selecting Plugins started its normal unfiltered marketplace snapshot; the command did not then deterministically enqueue a second marketplace fetch with a programmatic query.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After selecting Plugins, the new branch immediately sets the search input. Selection first makes PluginListWidget visible, whose refresh renders the home page and starts queryMarketplaceSnapshot(); the input change then schedules queryPluginSearch() 400 ms later.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 795 invokes `pane.setSearchQuery(searchQuery)` only after RIGHT line 793 has selected and made the target section visible, deterministically creating the second plugin-marketplace request path for searched deep links.
Findings.Title: Apply the plugin query before starting the default marketplace load
Findings.Impact: Opening `vscode://chat-customizations/open?page=plugins&search=...` from a cold cache can fetch every configured marketplace twice. Slow GitHub requests or clone-backed private marketplaces make the two requests overlap, wasting bandwidth/process work and competing with the request that supplies the visible search results.
Findings.Evidence: `selectSectionById` calls `updateContentVisibility`, which calls `PluginListWidget.setVisible(true)`; that calls `refresh()`, then `filterPlugins()`/`renderPluginHome()`, and `queryMarketplaceSnapshot()` calls `fetchMarketplacePlugins`. The added `pane.setSearchQuery(searchQuery)` changes the input, whose listener schedules `queryPluginSearch()` after 400 ms; that method independently calls `fetchMarketplacePlugins`. The search listener cancels only `marketplaceCts`, while the first request is owned by `marketplaceSnapshotCts`, and PluginMarketplaceService has a completed-result cache but no in-flight coalescing, so cold overlapping calls fan out independently across configured marketplaces.
Findings.Recommendation: Populate the PluginListWidget query before making the section visible (for example, pass the query through `selectSectionById` and set it before `updateContentVisibility`), or explicitly cancel/reuse the in-flight snapshot so the searched deep link performs only one marketplace fetch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup activates the new chat-customizations URL handler
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At BlockRestore, construction only resolves three services and registers one IURLHandler; no editor, search, filesystem, subprocess, IPC, or network work is started.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per workbench window: one contribution and one URL-handler registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and registration path were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Module evaluation cost was not measured, but the handler is small and its management dependency was already loaded by the existing AI customization contribution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression; the added blocking-phase work is constant and trivial.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, or Tools with an optional deep-link search
Scenarios.CriticalPath: URL parsing and the existing OpenEditor command must complete; section selection then applies one debounced in-memory filter. Editor construction also schedules its pre-existing migration-info refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute customization migration candidates through the existing migration services while constructing the management editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delayer-coalesced refresh per editor/context, with existing parallel work across enabled migration categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same OpenEditor command and editor construction performed this refresh before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduled during editor creation; this behavior already applies to every manual opening of the editor and is not added by search dispatch.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filtering scales with the already-loaded customization/tool collection; one filter is scheduled per handled URL.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search updates are debounced/coalesced by each widget. Migration categories are evaluated in the editor's existing coalesced refresh and internally use bounded category-level Promise.all fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor singleton and existing item models are reused on warm opens; no new search cache is introduced or defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setter listeners and editor selection flow were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Customization collection size varies, but the diff adds only one debounced local filter after the existing editor open.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; work is intentional, bounded to one URL action, and local after existing editor initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Plugins with a search query from a protocol URL
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The searched marketplace request supplies visible remote results. A default snapshot request is started first and is off the direct result path, but can overlap and contend with the searched request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch plugin definitions for every configured marketplace, with GitHub HTTP reads and possible clone-backed fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold searched deep link can cause two overlapping calls for each of M configured marketplaces; warm cache generally serves both locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The OpenEditor command selected Plugins but did not programmatically enqueue a searched fetch immediately after starting the default snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The second call is on the search-results critical path; the first is unnecessary for this queried view and competes for network/process resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M configured plugin marketplaces. On a cold request lasting over 400 ms, effective remote work grows from M fetches to 2M; each marketplace may issue HTTP reads or clone-backed discovery.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PluginMarketplaceService fans configured marketplaces out with Promise.all; the snapshot and searched fetch use distinct cancellation tokens and can run as two concurrent fan-outs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm completed marketplace cache entries avoid remote duplication. Cold misses are not in-flight-coalesced, so overlapping calls independently fetch; negative/failed results do not eliminate the overlap.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both fetch call paths, separate token ownership, delay, cache behavior, and lack of in-flight coalescing were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Impact depends on cache warmth, configured marketplace count, and whether requests finish within the 400 ms delay; slow/private marketplaces make the overlap most costly.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated boundary work; one low-severity finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open MCP Servers with a search query from a protocol URL
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selection makes the widget visible; applying the query immediately cancels the legacy snapshot token, and after 400 ms the searched gallery query supplies results. Connector refresh, when configured, remains the existing section-open behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query active/fallback MCP galleries for the search text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One delayed search, querying one or two deduplicated manifests; the just-started snapshot is canceled by the setter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual section opening loaded the snapshot; users could then type a query. The protocol now performs the same transition immediately with cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The searched query is on the result path; connector refresh may run independently as existing section behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the active and fallback gallery manifests per search, plus installed server cardinality for local filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Active/fallback gallery queries use existing bounded Promise.all/Promise.allSettled fan-out; the query setter cancels the snapshot request before scheduling the searched request.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget retains a gallery snapshot for local fallback; a non-empty query uses remote search only in legacy-gallery mode. Cancellation prevents sustained duplicate gallery work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call ordering and cancellation; lower only for transport-level cancellation timing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A transport may perform a small amount of work before observing immediate cancellation, but no sustained duplicate request was proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the existing cancellation lifecycle bounds the overlap and the cardinality is small.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Discover with a search query
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor shows the discovery page, then setSearchQuery cancels/reset any browse catalog request and schedules the searched marketplace query immediately; the searched page must return before remote results render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query enabled customization marketplace sources for the deep-link search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One current paged query, bounded by the existing filtered-backfill page cap and source configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening Discover could load the browse catalog; users manually entering search caused the same cancel-and-replace behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The searched catalog query is on the result-rendering critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One catalog page normally; existing typed-filter backfill can request up to its fixed maximum page count when media types cannot be represented directly.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One current catalog CancellationTokenSource; changing the query cancels and replaces prior work, while marketplace-service source fan-out remains internally managed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Empty browse pages use the existing browseCatalogCache. Searched queries reset catalog state and are not cached by this page; cancellation prevents stale browse work from committing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setQuery, reset, cancellation, scheduler, and page loop were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source latency and result-page count vary, but replacement is token-canceled and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the URL adds one intentional searched query using the page's established cancellation and paging bounds.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Migrations from a protocol URL
Scenarios.CriticalPath: OpenEditor constructs the existing editor and startCustomizationMigration awaits the coalesced migration-info refresh before rendering the dashboard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover migration candidates and target folders for enabled customization categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced computation for the current context, grouped by enabled category/target type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Passing the existing `{ migration: true }` target to OpenEditor already followed the same refresh/dashboard path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit migrations route waits for this existing computation before showing the dashboard.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories and their discovered customization/MCP candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing delayer coalesces refreshes; enabled categories and target-folder lookups use the editor's existing Promise.all grouping.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Context keys retain migration state for the current harness/session/project; a context change clears that state. The PR does not alter cache keys or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: command branch and migration refresh sequencing were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate counts vary by user configuration, but the PR does not change grouping, concurrency, or refresh frequency inside the migration implementation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; the protocol exposes an existing bounded workflow without changing its cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced startup activation, editor opening, local filtering, discovery/plugin/MCP marketplace requests, migration discovery, cache behavior, cancellation, and concurrency. Submitted one low-severity repeated-work finding for overlapping cold plugin marketplace fetches.
